items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: He used to be the drummer with Sonny Stitt and Wes Montgomery back in the day.

ctx.x: It can come from anywhere. It can come from any and all directions. Sometimes you hear the melody first, sometimes you hear a chord progression first, sometimes you hear a rhythmic beat that might influence it. I’ve written pieces from all directions. That particular piece came from a voicing that Frank Foster showed me on the piano for a big © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

band, or a saxophone section voicing, that’s very spread out. As a matter of fact it’s fifths between the baritone, second tenor, and then fifths between the first tenor, second alto and lead alto. And then you fit the trombones in between the spaces there. It’s a real big, thick sounding chord. And so he was showing me this voicing for the saxophones and I was checking it out and I said man, that’s nice. And then I kind of started moving things around here and said wait a minute, what’s this? And I said oh, oh,…
